findings.failure_scenario: For a user with `isPrimeAvailable === false` the whole ListItem (and badge) renders null, and for `isPrimeAvailable === true` the inner ternary still evaluates to null — `ETranslations.id_prime_soon` is unreachable from this page for every possible state. The retained badge block shows the refactor is internally inconsistent: either the intent was to keep the coming-soon teaser for non-Prime users (in which case the outer conditional wrongly hides the entire Prime entry, removing the teaser those users previously saw), or the badge block should have been deleted; as written it is leftover code that can never execute.
findings.summary: The inner conditional `{isPrimeAvailable ? null : <Badge>}` is dead code: the enclosing ternary renders this ListItem only when isPrimeAvailable is true, so the 'Prime coming soon' badge can never render in any state.

findings.failure_scenario: Before the change the item always rendered and `drillIn` genuinely varied with availability; after the change the prop can never be false where it is evaluated. The variable read misleads readers into thinking availability can vary inside the branch and obscures that the chevron/press affordance is unconditional here — the simpler form is the `drillIn` boolean shorthand.
findings.summary: `drillIn={isPrimeAvailable}` is now a constant `true` inside the branch guarded by `isPrimeAvailable`, so passing the variable is redundant and derivable state introduced by this change.
